name: destruction

attributes.attribute: concerns the destruction often by fire of a building
sacred vows the king failed to observe
named togail or togla in Irish

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Destructions form a category of Irish heroic tales. The Irish word is togail, also spelled togla. The heroic tales fall into several classes. The classes include visions, or Aisling. They include voyages. They include cattle raids. They include wooings. The tales concern the destruction of a building. Fire often brought the destruction. The class forms a recognized genre of the heroic tradition. The most famous tale is the Destruction of Da Derga's Hostel. That tale describes a king who failed to observe his sacred vows. His role required the vows, called geis. The breach led to his death. The tale shows the power of the vows. It links royal duty to a fatal consequence. The genre paints a grim picture. It shows how a transgression could bring ruin to a hall.
objective: Describe the destruction class of Irish heroic tales and its best-known example.
